info.title: Drive API
info.description:
Drive lets you understand your customers using the flags it compiles from data across every
source you bring in — not just transactions — build segments from those flags, and run
personalised campaigns against them. Drive works in a loop: **understand** your customers (via
the flags that make up Drive's criteria), **segment** them (Drive Segments API), and **engage**
them (Drive Campaigns API). Measuring a campaign's performance feeds back into segmentation, so
the next audience is sharper than the last.

Campaigns don't have to be built step by step, either: describe the outcome you want in plain
language and Drive's campaign agent finds the matching audience, writes the copy, generates the
artwork, and estimates the opportunity for you.

Segments V2 endpoints return non-standard vendor content types
(`application/vnd.bud.drive.notification+json`, `.criteria+json`, `.visualisation+json`,
`.criteria-options+json`) rather than plain `application/json` — check the `Content-Type` of
these responses rather than assuming JSON.

get.description:
Reports where a run has got to, and carries the finished campaign once it is done. `result` is null until the status is `completed`, so you poll this one endpoint throughout rather than switching to another when the run finishes.

A run belongs to the organisation that created it; another organisation's run is reported as not found rather than forbidden.

Once a run completes, pass `result.template_id` to Create Campaign as `template_id` to turn the drafted campaign into a live one.

parameters.name: generation_id
parameters.description: The ID returned when the campaign agent run was created.

status.description: Where the run has got to. `failed` is not final — a failed run may be retried automatically, so a later poll can return `running`.

result.title: Campaign Agent Result
result.description: The campaign a completed run produced. Null until the run reports `completed`.

template_id.description: The campaign template this run saved. Pass it as `template_id` to Create Campaign to turn the drafted campaign into a live one.

post.description:
Starts a campaign agent run and returns immediately. You describe the outcome you want in plain language, and the agent finds the audience that matches it, writes the campaign copy, generates the artwork and estimates the value of the opportunity.

Runs take minutes rather than seconds, so poll `GET /drive-api/v1/campaigns/agent/{generation_id}` every 10-15 seconds until the status is `completed`; that response then carries the campaign under `result`.

What the agent knows about your organisation — its context, tone of voice, branding and image style — is configured by Bud on your behalf, so most requests send nothing but the goal. Any of those can be overridden for a single run by sending it in the body; overrides apply to that run only and are never saved.

campaign_goal.description: The business goal the campaign should serve, in plain language.

context.title: Campaign Agent Override
context.description: Overrides your configured value for this run only. Leave it out to use what Bud has configured for you, or send an empty string to drop it for this run. Nothing sent here is saved against your organisation.

example.campaign_goal: find people who earn more than 2200 USD a month and are renters

OAuth2.description:
Authentication flow:

1. Perform OAuth2 Client Credentials authentication using API Credentials (`client_id`,`client_secret`) to obtain an `access_token` against `/v1/oauth/token` endpoint,
2. Use `access_token` as Bearer Authorisation for every other API request,
3. Include `X-Client-Id` (=client_id) within the header of every API request,
4. Note that some of the requests may also require `X-Customer-Id` to be provided within the request header.

### Examples
Obtain OAuth2 `access_token` and `refresh_token` using `grant_type=client_credentials` and HTTP Basic auth header

```
curl --basic --user {{client_id}}:{{client_secret}} \
  -X POST https://api-sandbox.thisisbud.com/v1/oauth/token \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/x-www-form-urlencoded' \
  -d grant_type=client_credentials
```

Successful response:
```
{
  "operation_id": "oauth_token_post",
  "data": {
    "access_token": "dd0c17e3fd6d2ce94aa091257a3ea393b4f9b5cf3d3e998f07dc9826da86ff15",
    "token_type": "bearer",
    "expires_in": 3600,
    "refresh_token": "fac32cca7559d9f6e8f1dfe9a99c71fa1dcfeb482bedf287d7934d2667ae54b3"
  }
}
```

Refresh `access_token` token using `refresh_token` against `/v1/oauth/token` endpoint with `grant_type=refresh_token`

```
curl -X POST \
  https://api-sandbox.thisisbud.com/v1/oauth/token \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/x-www-form-urlencoded' \
  -H 'X-Client-Id: {{client_id}}' \
  -d 'grant_type=refresh_token&refresh_token={{refresh_token}}'
```

Successful response:
```
{
    "operation_id": "oauth_token_post",
    "data": {
        "access_token": "cc0c17e3fd6d2ce94aa091257a3ea393b4f9b5cf3d3e998f07dc9826da86ff94",
        "token_type": "bearer",
        "expires_in": 3600,
        "refresh_token": "ffc30cca7559d9f6e8f1dfe9a99c71fa1dcfeb482bedf287d7934d2667ae54b3"
    }
}
```
